timeline_reviews.summary: Wrapper trajectory mirrors the parent work: executable probing, child activity, parent implementation, conflict detection, cleanup, verification, and final response.
Root parent probed argparse and Int8ul behavior, spawned a child, wrote the hierarchical solution, observed child-created flat files and overwritten entrypoint, repaired and verified.
First child probed executable behavior, spawned a nested probing child, then wrote a separate flat implementation and entrypoint before being interrupted by the root.
Nested child only probed CLI behavior and returned observations about equals syntax, duplicate flags, help text, unknown options, and reversed argument order.

timeline_reviews.summary: Wrapper trajectory shows a single actor probing executable behavior, writing the module hierarchy, verifying edge cases, setting executable mode, and finalizing.
Serial actor independently probed parser, range, and bytes literal edge cases, wrote one coherent hierarchy, ran Node checks, chmodded the entrypoint, and finished.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM `.mjs` requirement, local-only imports, `/output` deliverable placement, manual argparse-compatible `--a` and `--b` parsing, unsigned 8-bit build behavior, and Python bytes string formatting.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The root parent planned to own the implementation and verification but also spawned a `probe_cli` child; that child spawned a nested probing child and then independently implemented an overlapping solution in the same `/output` tree.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a hierarchical parser, Int8ul builder, Python bytes formatter, runner, and `test3.mjs`. The child separately wrote flat modules and its own `test3.mjs`, which temporarily became the observed entrypoint.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The root detected the child-created flat files and entrypoint content, deleted/recreated the entrypoint, removed the flat modules, and delivered the parent hierarchy listed in final.txt.
parallel.verification: The parent compared normal output and argparse-like errors against the executable, initially saw help and error diffs while the child entrypoint was present, then re-ran valid, help, missing, unknown, underscore, equals, duplicate, and invalid-int checks after cleanup.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official functional defect remained at closure; the unresolved process defect was the recovered shared-output overwrite and the interrupted child work that was not part of final delivery.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM `.mjs`, local imports, `/output` hierarchy, manual argv parsing, no external dependencies, Int8ul range behavior, and Python bytes literal formatting requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept investigation, implementation, integration, verification, executable permission, and delivery in one actor without delegation or shared workspace ownership splits.
serial.implementation: Wrote `pathUtils.mjs`, `parseTest3Args.mjs`, `buildTwoFieldStruct.mjs`, `pythonBytesLiteral.mjs`, `runTest3.mjs`, and `test3.mjs` as one coherent hierarchy.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all modules through one entrypoint, marked `test3.mjs` executable, listed the final file tree, and returned the generated layout in final.txt.
serial.verification: Probed executable behavior extensively, including samples, help, missing args, invalid ints, unknown args, duplicate flags, range failures, quote selection, escape bytes, and then verified the Node entrypoint on representative cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official functional defect or visible coordination issue remained at closure; the serial solution passed all 126 official samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized and implemented the ESM module, manual CLI, Int8ul, bytes formatting, and local-only requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and explicitly probed extra bytes literal quoting and escape cases before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the task requirements sufficiently for 126 of 126 official tests; serial's probing was more centralized, while parallel split some probing across children.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned a complete implementation while a child also proceeded from probing into an overlapping implementation and entrypoint write.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor own probing, implementation, integration, verification, chmod, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping implementation ownership in `/output`; serial had a single coherent owner, avoiding ownership interference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child agents received enough task context to probe and implement, but the run did not establish an effective shared file ownership boundary for `/output/test3.mjs`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need a cross-agent interface or file ownership contract because one actor made all decisions and writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference was not missing task context but missing write isolation for the shared deliverable; taxonomy precedence maps the realized event to a write label.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final parallel artifact used parser, construct, format, runner, and entry modules; an intermediate child implementation used a competing flat module set.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a single hierarchy with runtime path utilities, CLI parser, construct builder, bytes formatter, app runner, and entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final solutions were functionally equivalent but structurally different; parallel had to discard a child-created flat implementation before finalizing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The nested child returned a probing result to the first child; the first child was later interrupted after writing conflicting output, and the root did not need to join that implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and moved directly from local checks to implementation, verification, chmod, and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child activity and an interrupted child after conflict detection; serial had no retrieval or join risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Shared `/output` writes produced competing flat and hierarchical modules, and the parent saw the child-owned entrypoint content before cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's shared state was stable: one actor wrote the hierarchy and final file listing without competing writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main task-solving process difference: parallel recovered from a deliverable overwrite and serial never encountered one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran parity comparisons, observed diffs while the overwritten entrypoint was active, fixed the tree, and re-ran checks that matched stdout, stderr, and exit codes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran extensive executable probes and Node checks including samples, parser errors, range errors, quotes, escapes, chmod, and final file listing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted only after local verification and both passed official tests; parallel spent verification effort detecting and correcting its coordination-induced file state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within budget but used three subagents, 66 LLM requests, and additional cleanup/reverification after the overwrite episode.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed within budget with no subagents, 21 LLM requests, one coherent implementation pass, and no cleanup of competing agents' files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more coordination and verification budget but still had enough time to repair and pass; serial was shorter and simpler.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations pass 126 of 126 test cases, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel used children and had to recover from a child-overwritten entrypoint and duplicate flat modules, while serial stayed single-owner and avoided that recovery work.
parallel_contributors: Parallel child activity helped probe behavior but also created overlapping `/output` writes.
The root parent detected the duplicate flat module tree and repaired the entrypoint before final verification.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all probing, implementation, verification, and delivery in one actor.
Serial explicitly checked quote and escape bytes formatting cases before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final module names and hierarchy differ between modes, but both satisfy the ESM and local-import requirements.
Parallel's final summary claims Python bytes formatting coverage; serial's trajectory shows more explicit quote-selection probing, but the evaluator accepted both.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process episode, not a failure explanation
